63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment
64: func diff(got, want string) string {
65: 	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
66: 	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
67: 	for i := 0; ; i++ {
68: 		switch {
69: 		case i < len(g) && i < len(w):
70: 			if g[i] == w[i] {
71: 				continue
72: 			}
73: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- first difference in line %d:\n"+
74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])
78: 		case i < len(w):
79: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d correct lines, want %d more lines:\n"+
80: 				"-- want next: %q\n", i, len(w)-i, w[i])
81: 		default:
82: 			return "no differences found"
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: }

Wait, there's still a bug: in verse 2 (spider), the chain is "She swallowed the spider to catch the fly." — my loop at i=1 generates "She swallowed the spider to catch the fly that wriggled..." — no wait: the i>0 branch uses animals[i-1] as the catch target with the wriggled suffix. For i=1 (spider), animals[i-1] = fly, so it generates "She swallowed the spider to catch the fly that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her." — that's wrong! The expected value is "She swallowed the spider to catch the fly." without the suffix.

The wriggled suffix is only appended when the catch target is a spider (index 1). So the rule is: "She swallowed the X to catch the Y[ that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her.]", and the suffix is only used when Y is a spider.

Therefore the loop is: for i := v-1; i >= 0; i-- { if i == 0 { "She swallowed the fly to catch the fly." } else { target := animals[i-1].name; if target == "spider" { target += " that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her" }; "She swallowed the X to catch the target." } }.

And verse 1: the loop should not be executed at all. The current code has `if i == 0 { if v == 1 { continue } ... }` — for v=1, i=0, it continues, so no problem. But wait, for v=1, the loop runs with i=0 and continues — OK.
